summary: 3 blocking spec review findings should be applied: preserve missing-acceptance blockers through scope filtering, define registry post-hook behavior, and cover task-scoped impl review.

items.title: Scope filtering can discard required blocking findings
items.rationale: The finding identifies a real contradiction between missing-acceptance blockers and file-path-only scope filtering. The spec must define how requirement-level blockers survive filtering.
items.evidence: spec-review.json blockingFindings[0] shows that a missing acceptance requirement may not have a touched file path but still must block PASS.

items.title: Impl review FAIL transition omits the registry post hook
items.rationale: The finding names an existing transition owner that can advance the step independently of run-review parsing. The spec must require the registry post hook to use structured verdicts.
items.evidence: spec-review.json blockingFindings[1] states that `FLOW_COMMANDS.run.review.post` may mark impl review done unless it consumes the new structured verdict.

items.title: Task-scoped impl review compatibility is unspecified
items.rationale: The same review command has a task-scoped `--task-spec` path, so the spec must either include that path in the structured contract or explicitly preserve separate behavior.
items.evidence: spec-review.json blockingFindings[2] identifies the task-scoped path and stale task review prompt as a conflict with the shared command behavior.
